When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Contrarian score **100/100**, STRONG BUY vs Regime state **61**, RISK OFF BIAS with **3** signals aligned, macro regime CONTRACTION at **70%**
The contrarian gauge measures how stretched fear is. The regime model measures what the economy and credit are doing. Trust the regime model for direction and size. Treat the contrarian score as a trigger that only counts once the VIX term structure and credit stop deteriorating.
⚠ These two disagree: Divergence composite zone CALM, with **39.5%** of pairs diverging vs Mother jaws score **100**, with six pairs in DEEP DIVERG
The composite averages **43** pairs, so a handful of extreme pairs get diluted. The six deep pairs sit in rates, vol and FX, which are the places stress shows first. Trust the jaws for early warning and the composite for how broad the stress is.
⚠ These two disagree: Two confluences active that need VIX backwardation (T1 x HYG, T1 x JPY) vs VIX spike detector shows backwardation_active false
The confluence flags and the detector disagree on whether the VIX curve is inverted. Trust the detector for the curve itself. Read the two confluences as credit and yen stress that is already live, with the VIX leg still missing.

The call is defensive with a contrarian itch. Crash Index is 4/10 (WARNING, active surveillance), regime state is 61 in TRANSITION, and 3 risk off signals line up. The macro regime is CONTRACTION at 70% confidence. Against that, the contrarian score is 100. You have a market where the slow indicators say contraction and the fast fear gauge says capitulation.

For positioning, the regime model sets the direction and the contrarian score sets the watch list. The Nasdaq 100 gave up 4.9% in 5 days while the Dow lost only 0.9%, so the pain sits in growth and not in defensives. That favors holding gross exposure below normal and keeping new buys small and staged. Two confluences are active out of three, covering credit stress (HYG) and yen safe haven flow (JPY). Those are the channels a contraction regime uses to spread.

The main risk is that the VIX curve inverts. Backwardation is off today and the spike tier is 1 of 4 with a 50% probability reading, with skew already active. If backwardation turns on and the tier climbs, the risk off stance hardens and the contrarian buy is early. If HYG stabilizes and the six deep divergence pairs start to re-correlate, the contrarian read takes over and you can add.

Dow Theory generalized · cross-asset divergences
Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence means two assets that usually move together have started to move apart. Correlation drift is the size of that change: how tightly the pair moved together over the past year versus how it moves now.

The composite zone reads CALM, with 39.5% of 43 pairs diverging and a net bias of -7 (5 bearish, 12 bullish). The mother jaws score is 100, and that is where the information sits.

AUD/JPY drifted from +0.58 to -0.25, so the classic risk appetite pair has stopped confirming equities. ETH/BTC flipped from -0.68 to +0.39.

VIX versus realized vol moved from -0.48 to +0.09, which means fear and actual movement no longer track each other. The 10y minus 2y spread went from -0.53 to +0.25.

MOVE went from +0.33 to -0.28. SPY and TLT correlation collapsed from +0.76 to +0.03, so bonds no longer hedge stocks the way they did.

The bond hedge being weaker matters most for sizing: if equities fall, you cannot count on Treasuries to cushion it.

Asia · Europe · US · Crypto 24/7 — lead-lag detection
Cross-Region Surveillance
Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

Asia shows the widest spread: Hong Kong's HSI is up 8.0% in 5 days while Korea's KS11 is down 9.3%. That gap means capital is rotating inside the region, with China related assets bid and Korean tech and export exposure sold.

Europe is steady: France's FCHI is up 3.0% and the STOXX 50 is up 0.4%. The US is the weak link, with the Dow down 0.9% and the Nasdaq 100 down 4.9%.

Crypto is soft too, with ETH down 1.5% and SOL down 4.6%. Korea's drop and the Nasdaq 100's slide point the same way: semiconductor and growth exposure is the pressure point.

For today's US session, expect growth to stay heavy and defensives to hold up better. A Nasdaq 100 bounce that Korea does not confirm should be sold, not chased.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 4/10 · WARNING — 3+ signals, active surveillance
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

Crash Index sits at 4/10 and the VIX Spike Detector is at tier 1 of 4 (BROAD) with a 50% probability. These two agree more than they differ.

Both say stress is building without a full break. Skew is active, which means traders are paying up for downside protection.

Backwardation is off, so the front of the VIX curve is not yet screaming. That combination describes a market hedging ahead of a move.

It has not yet panicked. Trust the options market for timing, because it moves before price does.

The flip is backwardation switching on. That would turn a hedged market into a forced one, and the 50% probability would need a re-read.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 4/10 — a few early signals are stirring; watch whether more line up.

The stress (HYG/IEF, VIX3M/VIX, STLFSI4) ring at 5-30 days. The triggers (SPY -2% in 5d, VIX +30% in 3d) are short-term breakouts. For a tactical decision: 3+ signals simultaneously aligned = real probability of stress, never on isolated signal (framework rule).

How to read
Aggregation of all panel signals across the 4 cross-asset buckets. RISK-ON = risk appetite (cyclical, equity, EM). RISK-OFF = flight to defensives (TLT, gold, JPY). STRESS = liquidity tension (HYG, MOVE, STLFSI). TOPPING = end-of-cycle signals (concentration, breadth narrowing, defensives leading). Doctrine: a single signal = noise. 3+ aligned in one bucket = real confirmed regime.

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
